title: Single-photon addition to multimode quantum fields at telecom wavelengths using lithium niobate and its doped variants
authors: Naveen V, Nicolas Treps, Raghavan G, Valentina Parigi, Srinivasan K
abstract: Multimode spectro-temporal non-Gaussian quantum states of light play a crucial role in continuous-variable quantum information processing. In particular, the non-Gaussian quantum states generated through a single-photon addition (SPA) to multimode quantum fields at telecommunication wavelengths constitute a useful resource for quantum technologies. We present a detailed theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of single-photon addition (SPA) and mode-selective single-photon addition (MSSPA) to a multimode quantum field at telecommunication wavelengths. The analysis is performed for congruently grown lithium niobate (LN), $5\%$ MgO-doped lithium niobate (MgO:LN) and various concentrations of ZnO-doped lithium niobate (ZnO:LN) bulk crystals. We investigate MSSPA using type-II parametric down-conversion (PDC) and SPA using the type-I PDC processes. We further present spectro-temporal mode-selective SPA at the telecom wavelength using $5\%$ MgO:LN for temperatures ranging from $0^\circ C$ to $15^\circ C$. In addition, we perform simulations to investigate SPA based on the noncollinear type-I PDC configuration. These theoretical results identify optimal experimental conditions and phase-matching parameters to achieve SPA and mode-selective SPA for LN-based crystals, providing a potential platform for non-Gaussian quantum state engineering at telecommunication wavelengths, mainly at $1550$ nm.
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive theoretical analysis detailing how to generate single-photon-added, spectro-temporally multimode quantum states using nonlinear crystals like Lithium Niobate. By modeling the parametric down-conversion process, the authors identify optimal doping levels and operational conditions to achieve high-purity quantum states at crucial telecom wavelengths (1550 nm). This work establishes a viable platform for quantum state engineering in integrated photonics.
main_problem: The paper addresses the generation of spectro-temporal non-Gaussian quantum states, specifically through single-photon addition (SPA), to multimode quantum fields at telecom wavelengths.
main_result: The authors established a theoretical framework demonstrating that SPA can be achieved using lithium niobate (LN) and its doped variants, identifying optimal conditions for high spectral purity at 1550 nm.
method: The analysis involves detailed theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of the parametric down-conversion (PDC) process, utilizing the Joint Spectral Amplitude (JSA) and the Schmidt number ($K$) as key diagnostics.
model_or_system: The physical platform is nonlinear bulk crystals, specifically Lithium Niobate (LN) and its MgO:LN and ZnO:LN doped variants. The process modeled is Spontaneous Parametric Down-Conversion (PDC), which generates the quantum states.
key_observables: Joint Spectral Amplitude (JSA), Schmidt number ($K$), signal and idler spectra, and the satisfaction of Phase-Matching and Group Velocity Matching (GVM) conditions.
important_parameters: Telecom wavelengths (especially 1550 nm), crystal doping concentrations (e.g., 5% MgO:LN), and temperature variations ($0^\circ	ext{C}$ to $15^\circ	ext{C}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on theoretical approximations, such as Taylor expansions, and distinguishes between two regimes: those satisfying GVM and those that bypass this strict requirement.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the quantum state generation, the phase-matching and GVM condition plots for different crystal cuts, and the resulting signal/idler spectra confirming the achievable purity ($K$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first analyzing the general requirements for mode-selective SPA (requiring both phase-matching and GVM), noting limitations in initial materials (congruent LN), and then developing advanced theoretical approaches (noncollinear PDC) to realize the process under optimal conditions for doped LN crystals.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems as it provides a detailed, materials-specific roadmap for engineering non-Gaussian quantum resources necessary for advanced quantum information protocols.
